column3: I believe the role of physicists will change significantly due to the advancement of AI.

column1: Function 1: Problem finding and research formulation
column3: With the emergence of AI, what makes a good physicist is shifting from being able to calculate towards asking the right questions.

column1: Function 1: Problem finding and research formulation
column3: Even with AI, the scientist’s defining work remains asking the right questions and connecting ideas.

column1: Function 1: Problem finding and research formulation
column3: Deciding which scientific questions are worth pursuing should remain a researcher’s responsibility.

column1: Function 2: Critical evaluation and oversight of AI
column3: Students should learn from human advisors how to evaluate the work of AI, including where it fails.

column1: Function 2: Critical evaluation and oversight of AI
column3: As AI increases the speed at which research results can be produced, science should prioritize verification.

column1: Function 2: Critical evaluation and oversight of AI
column3: As AI advances, the most important role of physicists will be to determine how to direct and use AI.

column1: Function 2: Critical evaluation and oversight of AI
column3: When using AI-generation, human researchers should bear the ultimate responsibility for the correctness of the results.

column1: Function 3: Building skill competence before AI
column3: Students should be prevented from using AI until they have learned the fundamentals.

column1: Function 3: Building skill competence before AI
column3: You have to be able to do the mathematics yourself, or you are not really a scientist.

column1: Function 3: Building skill competence before AI
column3: The slow struggle of doing the work yourself is how you truly learn, and skipping this through AI is detrimental.

column1: Function 3: Building skill competence before AI
column3: Students with strong prior knowledge and skills benefit more from using AI than those without strong preparation for the field.
